Author: Sandro
Name: NahjaUI
Punchline: A complete, modular interface for Final Fantasy XIV.
Description:
NahjaUI gives the game a clean, consistent interface that you build piece by piece. Switch on only what you want: everything else stays exactly as the game made it.

HUD bars: your parameter bar, target, target of target, focus target and party list.
Progress bars: your casts and your target's, with a slidecast marker, plus a global cooldown bar that shows the queue and weave windows.
Job gauges, status effects, nameplates and enmity list, each one with its own style.
Trackers: pick the enhancements, enfeeblements and cooldowns you want to see. Every job comes with ready-made presets.
Profiles: save, copy and share your whole setup.

Type /nui to open it.
Changelog: New: Interface scale slider (Appearance). One shared position for every job, with a Use a different position for this job checkbox; tracker groups (Rotation, CDs, Defensive CDs) share their position too. Cutscene icon on the party list and on party nameplates. Preview mode: every settings page shows a sample of what you are editing, marked PREVIEW and switched off in combat, and it ignores the show-when conditions so you can always place it. Tooltip page shows an example tooltip. Fixes: nameplates are never cut by game windows, and the quest list and the minimap no longer cut the HUD. Streamer Mode keeps the job names of enemy players in PvP. Dead party members keep only their raise statuses. Search lists of the tracker editor close when you pick an entry. Sharper text. Enmity list no longer cut by the alliance list.
